meta.title: THE BRIDGE — explore your path
meta.description: A platform that helps teenagers, students and adults explore possible paths through their own answers, real human stories and small experiments.

footer.tagline: A bridge between the questions of young people and the experience of those who have already found their path.

hero.title: Your future doesn't have to be figured out today.
hero.lead: Explore who you could become through your own answers, real human stories and small experiments — without pressure or ready-made answers.
hero.note: You can start right away, no sign-up needed.

problem.title: Paths are often chosen at random.
problem.lead: At 16 or 17 you are expected to make a decision that feels final. Few people get the chance to understand themselves or try anything in practice first.
problem.p1Text: A major is picked before you know what you actually enjoy.
problem.p2Text: You only see a handful of familiar jobs, and real human stories are scarce.
problem.p3Text: Family expectations and fear of mistakes drown out your own interests.

how.title: Four steps you can take at your own pace.
how.step1Text: Answer questions about your interests, values and what gives you energy.
how.step2Text: Read the stories of people who started with similar questions.
how.step3Text: Get a breakdown of which directions are worth exploring and why — no verdicts.
how.step4Text: Run a small experiment and test an interest in practice.

stories.title: Paths are rarely straight.
stories.lead: Stories of people who changed direction, doubted and found their own way. Every story is labelled with where it comes from — we never pass off examples as real lives.
stories.kindsLabel: Every story carries one of four labels:
stories.verifiedDesc: The source has been checked via a link.
stories.documentedDesc: Told publicly — in an interview, book or article.
stories.userDesc: Sent by a community member and reviewed by moderators.
stories.demoDesc: A fictional example that shows how the platform works.

try.title: A small experiment beats endless doubt.
try.lead: Short tasks that let you feel a profession from the inside in one evening, not four years of study.
try.example2: Work through a real case like a lawyer

opportunities.title: Programmes, scholarships and internships in one place.
opportunities.lead: We collect real programmes with official links and the date they were last checked.
opportunities.note: Always confirm deadlines and requirements on the programme's official website.

community.title: A project made by people, not algorithms.
community.lead: THE BRIDGE is an educational project run by a team of ambassadors. We build a bridge between the questions of young people and the experience of those who have already found their path.
community.ambassadorsText: The team the project grew out of.

explore.introPoint2: You can skip personal ones — we explain why we ask.
explore.introPoint3: Answers save automatically, so you can come back later.

explore.completeLead: You have covered the essentials. Now you can build your personal report — not a verdict and not a prediction, but a map of directions worth exploring.
explore.missingTitle: A few more questions to go
explore.missingLead: Without these blocks the report would be too vague:

A1.title: How old are you?
A1.hint: Pick a range — an exact age is not needed.
A1.whyWeAsk: Age changes which questions and examples help most: a school student and someone changing careers face different choices.

A2.title: What are you doing right now?
A2.whyWeAsk: So we do not ask too much: a school student does not need questions about jobs, and someone working does not need questions about choosing a school.

options.other: Something else (a pause, searching, parental leave…)

A3.title: Which country and city are you from?
A3.hint: Optional. You can write only the country, or skip.
A3.whyWeAsk: Opportunities and scholarships often depend on the country. This is only used to suggest options that fit.

A4.title: What are you studying, and how is it going?
A4.hint: Write your field and a few words on whether you like it. Optional.

A5.title: What are you doing at the moment?
A5.hint: A job, a side job, a pause — whatever is true. Optional.

A6.title: How clear is your idea of what to do after school?
A6.hint: An honest answer beats a “right” one.

options.some: I have a couple of options but I am not sure
options.pause: I want to pause first and look around

B1.title: What draws you in?
B1.hint: Pick up to five topics or activities. There are no wrong answers.
B1.whyWeAsk: This is the basis for ideas and experiments. Choose what resonates, not what you “should” choose.

options.unsure: Not sure yet — a bit of everything

B2.title: What could you talk about for hours, or what do you teach yourself?
B2.hint: Topics, channels, books, hobbies — anything that comes to mind.

B3.title: What absorbs you so much that you lose track of time?
B3.hint: Any activity, even if it feels unserious.

B4.title: What would you do if nothing limited you — money, other people's expectations, fear?
B4.hint: Dream a little. You can be bolder here than usual.

C1.title: Are you more comfortable working alone or in a team?
C1.hint: Pick 1 to 5 for what is closer. There are no right answers.
C1.whyWeAsk: This is not a grade or a label, just a hint about which working environment might suit you.

C2.title: How much do you enjoy talking with lots of people at work?

C3.title: What is closer to you: practice or theory?
C3.whyWeAsk: It helps us pick experiments in a format that suits you. Not a label, just a guide.

C4.title: How do you feel when a task is hard and there are no clear instructions?
C4.scaleMax: I enjoy figuring it out myself

C5.title: What matters more to you in work: stability or experimenting?
C5.whyWeAsk: So we understand which directions and first steps feel comfortable, and which are too risky for you right now.

D1.title: Which of these have you already done?
D1.hint: You can pick several. If none yet, that is perfectly fine.

D2.title: Tell us about one such experience: what did you do, and what are you proud of?
D2.hint: A couple of sentences is enough.

D3.title: Was there an experience that changed how you see something, or a difficulty you overcame?
D3.hint: Optional, but stories like these say a lot about you.

E1.title: What is hardest for you about choosing a path?
E1.whyWeAsk: So the advice reflects what actually gets in the way, not just a list of professions.

options.noIdea: I do not know what I like
options.wrongChoice: I am afraid of choosing wrong
options.noTalent: I feel I have no special talent
options.tooLate: I feel it is already too late

E2.title: Do you feel pressure from your family about your path?
E2.whyWeAsk: This is personal. We ask so we do not give advice that is hard to use at home.

E2b.title: How does it show up?
E2b.hint: Pick the closest one. You can skip this.
E2b.whyWeAsk: This is also personal. Answer only if you want to — it helps us see which steps are realistic.

options.profession: They want me to pick a specific profession
options.closeToHome: They want me to stay close to home
options.income: They expect me to start earning soon

E3.title: Have you already chosen something that now feels like it is not yours?
E3.hint: A major, a university, a job — anything.

E3b.title: What exactly does not fit?
E3b.hint: What does not resonate, and maybe what you still like about it?

E4.title: Do you sometimes feel you have no particular talent?
E4.hint: There is no right answer — many people feel this way.

F1.title: What matters most to you in your future work and life?
F1.whyWeAsk: Values help find a path that fits you, not “everyone”.

F2.title: What does “success” mean to you?
F2.hint: In your own words, no polished phrasing needed.

F3.title: What problems in the world or around you would you like to solve?

F4.title: What would make your life feel meaningful?

G1.title: Are there real-life limits that affect your choice?
G1.hint: Optional. Pick up to three that matter most.
G1.whyWeAsk: To suggest realistic steps and opportunities, such as scholarships. You can skip this.

G2.title: How are you placed for paying for study?
G2.whyWeAsk: So we understand whether scholarships and grants matter for you. It only affects the suggestions.

options.selfFunded: I can pay, or my family can help
options.partial: I can cover part of it
options.needScholarship: I need a scholarship or grant

G3.title: How easy is access to education where you live?
G3.whyWeAsk: It decides whether in-person options fit or starting online makes more sense.

G4.title: Which languages do you speak?
G4.hint: You can pick several. You can skip this.
G4.whyWeAsk: Language affects study and work opportunities, including abroad.

G5.title: How much time per week can you give to something new?
G5.whyWeAsk: So experiments and the plan are doable, not one more source of stress.

G6.title: How willing are you to move?
G6.whyWeAsk: Study options and opportunities depend on it.

options.city: I need to stay in my city

G7.title: What family responsibilities do you have?
G7.whyWeAsk: So the steps are realistic and do not need more time than you have.

options.some: Some, but I still have time
options.main: They take most of my time

report.explorationNote: This is exploration, not prediction. There are no verdicts here about who you should be — only hypotheses you can test in practice.
report.loadingNote: This usually takes up to a minute. No rush.
report.errorLead: Your answers are saved. Try again — it usually helps.
report.notFoundLead: It may have been built on another device, or the data was cleared. Take the questionnaire — a new report takes about a minute.
report.s3: Things you might not have noticed

report.s5Lead: People in similar circumstances. Closeness is approximate — it shows what is alike and what is not.
report.s5Empty: No similar stories yet. Check the stories section later — it keeps growing.
report.s7Lead: Small trials that will make it clearer what you enjoy in practice.
report.s8Lead: Tick off what you've done, change and add steps — the plan is yours.
report.activities: What people do day to day
report.planEmpty: Empty for now — add the first step.
